name: Jonah
charge: Rising up to flee unto Tarshish from the presence of the Lord instead of going to Nineveh to cry against it
summary: The word of the Lord sent Jonah the son of Amittai to cry against Nineveh, and he rose up to flee to Tarshish from the presence of the Lord (Jonah 1:1-3). The storm found him asleep in the ship; he confessed he was the cause and was cast into the sea, and the Lord prepared a great fish in which he lay three days and three nights, praying, until he was put out on dry land (Jonah 1:4-17; Jonah 2:1-10). Sent the second time he went and cried against the city, and when the Lord spared it he was angry; the Lord reproved him with the gourd, and Christ made his three days the sign given to His generation (Jonah 3:1-4; Jonah 4:1-11; Matthew 12:39-40).
offenseFull: Jonah the son of Amittai prophesied in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, who restored Israel’s border by his word (2 Kings 14:25). The word came to him to go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it, for its wickedness had come up before the Lord (Jonah 1:1-2). Christians read Ninevites and think Assyrians, the Luke 11 teaching says, but the Ninevites to whom Jonah was a sign were the captives of the ten tribes led into Nineveh, as Tobit of Naphtali shows, who was carried there and heard Jonah and took heed (Tobit 1:1-3; Tobit 14:8); the study note on Acts 1 likewise says Jonah preached to Nineveh, where the northern kingdom was exiled. Our people in Nineveh were observing lying vanities, one class says, as they keep Christmas and a white Jesus today (Jonah 2:8).

Jonah said no, as the teacher puts it: he rose up to flee to Tarshish from the presence of the Lord, went down to Joppa, found a ship, paid the fare and went aboard (Jonah 1:3). The study note on Genesis 10 places Tarshish in Spain, first among the merchants of Tyre (Ezekiel 27:12); one history teaching reads from a book that Jonah looked to it as a safe haven where Hebrew traders had been since Solomon’s time, and another says most place it at Sicily. Two classes say he fled because he was afraid of the people of Nineveh; he himself later says he fled because he knew the Lord was gracious and merciful and would relent (Jonah 4:2), and the teaching adds that he feared being taken for a false prophet. Both can stand; like Adam, one class says, he tried to hide.

The Lord sent a great wind and the ship was near breaking; the mariners cried each to his own god, and Jonah lay fast asleep in the sides of the ship (Jonah 1:4-5). The study note calls him the picture of the slack spirit, asleep while the ship breaks, and America the spiritual ship going down with our people asleep in it. The lot fell on Jonah, and he confessed he was a Hebrew who feared the Lord, the God of heaven who made the sea and the dry land (Jonah 1:7-10).
judgmentFull: He told them to throw him into the sea, for the storm was on his account (Jonah 1:11-12). That is accountability and integrity, the teaching says, owning that you are the cause, the opposite of Achan, whose hidden sin troubled the camp (Joshua 7:1). They rowed hard, prayed not to be charged with innocent blood, and cast him in, and the sea ceased her raging (Jonah 1:13-16). The Lord had prepared a great fish and Jonah was in its belly three days and three nights (Jonah 1:17). He cried to the Lord out of the belly of hell, which the teaching explains is the grave; cast out of His sight, he would look again toward the holy temple and pay what he had vowed (Jonah 2:1-9). The man who fled the Lord now sought Him, as in their affliction they will seek Him early (Hosea 5:15); in the fish, one class says, he repented of his fear and his doubt, and the teaching reads his rising from the pit as pointing to Christ, whose soul would not be left in the grave (Psalm 16:10).

The word came the second time, and he went and cried what he was given, that in forty days Nineveh would be overthrown (Jonah 3:1-4). When the Lord spared the city he was very angry and asked to die (Jonah 4:1-3). Jonah had an attitude problem, one class says, self-willed, mad that God did not destroy the people, like James and John wanting fire from heaven (Luke 9:54-55). With the gourd, the worm and the east wind the Lord showed him that he pitied a plant he had not laboured for, and asked whether He should not spare Nineveh (Jonah 4:4-11). Your spirit is not right, the teacher says; we do not preach for our own glory, and His thoughts are not our thoughts (Isaiah 55:8). The Lord held off because His people were there, the Luke 11 teaching says, but the word still stood and the city was destroyed (Tobit 14:4).

Christ gave that generation no sign but the sign of Jonas: as Jonah was three days and three nights in the fish, the Son of man would be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth, and one greater than Jonah was there (Matthew 12:39-41). Three days and three nights, the teaching says, rules out Good Friday to Sunday. Jonah is actually about us, one class says: the God who heard him in the fish does not change (Malachi 3:6), so pray.

text.text: Now the word of the Lord came unto Jonah the son of Amittai, saying,
Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it; for their wickedness is come up before me.

But Jonah rose up to flee unto Tarshish from the presence of the Lord, and went down to Joppa; and he found a ship going to Tarshish: so he paid the fare thereof, and went down into it, to go with them unto Tarshish from the presence of the Lord.
But the Lord sent out a great wind into the sea, and there was a mighty tempest in the sea, so that the ship was like to be broken.

Then the mariners were afraid, and cried every man unto his god, and cast forth the wares that were in the ship into the sea, to lighten it of them. But Jonah was gone down into the sides of the ship; and he lay, and was fast asleep.
So the shipmaster came to him, and said unto him, What meanest thou, O sleeper? arise, call upon thy God, if so be that God will think upon us, that we perish not.
And they said every one to his fellow, Come, and let us cast lots, that we may know for whose cause this evil is upon us. So they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Jonah.
Then said they unto him, Tell us, we pray thee, for whose cause this evil is upon us; What is thine occupation? and whence comest thou? what is thy country? and of what people art thou?
And he said unto them, I am an Hebrew; and I fear the Lord, the God of heaven, which hath made the sea and the dry land.
Then were the men exceedingly afraid, and said unto him, Why hast thou done this? For the men knew that he fled from the presence of the Lord, because he had told them.
Then said they unto him, What shall we do unto thee, that the sea may be calm unto us? for the sea wrought, and was tempestuous.
And he said unto them, Take me up, and cast me forth into the sea; so shall the sea be calm unto you: for I know that for my sake this great tempest is upon you.
Nevertheless the men rowed hard to bring it to the land; but they could not: for the sea wrought, and was tempestuous against them.

Wherefore they cried unto the Lord, and said, We beseech thee, O Lord, we beseech thee, let us not perish for this man’s life, and lay not upon us innocent blood: for thou, O Lord, hast done as it pleased thee.
So they took up Jonah, and cast him forth into the sea: and the sea ceased from her raging.
Then the men feared the Lord exceedingly, and offered a sacrifice unto the Lord, and made vows.
Now the Lord had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah. And Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.
Then Jonah prayed unto the Lord his God out of the fish’s belly,
And said, I cried by reason of mine affliction unto the Lord, and he heard me; out of the belly of hell cried I, and thou heardest my voice.
For thou hadst cast me into the deep, in the midst of the seas; and the floods compassed me about: all thy billows and thy waves passed over me.
Then I said, I am cast out of thy sight; yet I will look again toward thy holy temple.
The waters compassed me about, even to the soul: the depth closed me round about, the weeds were wrapped about my head.
I went down to the bottoms of the mountains; the earth with her bars was about me for ever: yet hast thou brought up my life from corruption, O Lord my God.
When my soul fainted within me I remembered the Lord: and my prayer came in unto thee, into thine holy temple.
They that observe lying vanities forsake their own mercy.
But I will sacrifice unto thee with the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay that that I have vowed. Salvation is of the Lord.
And the Lord spake unto the fish, and it vomited out Jonah upon the dry land.
And the word of the Lord came unto Jonah the second time, saying,
Arise, go unto Nineveh, that great city, and preach unto it the preaching that I bid thee.
So Jonah arose, and went unto Nineveh, according to the word of the Lord. Now Nineveh was an exceeding great city of three days’ journey.
And Jonah began to enter into the city a day’s journey, and he cried, and said, Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown.
But it displeased Jonah exceedingly, and he was very angry.

And he prayed unto the Lord, and said, I pray thee, O Lord, was not this my saying, when I was yet in my country? Therefore I fled before unto Tarshish: for I knew that thou art a gracious God, and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repentest thee of the evil.
Therefore now, O Lord, take, I beseech thee, my life from me; for it is better for me to die than to live.
Then said the Lord, Doest thou well to be angry?
So Jonah went out of the city, and sat on the east side of the city, and there made him a booth, and sat under it in the shadow, till he might see what would become of the city.
And the Lord God prepared a gourd, and made it to come up over Jonah, that it might be a shadow over his head, to deliver him from his grief. So Jonah was exceeding glad of the gourd.
But God prepared a worm when the morning rose the next day, and it smote the gourd that it withered.

And it came to pass, when the sun did arise, that God prepared a vehement east wind; and the sun beat upon the head of Jonah, that he fainted, and wished in himself to die, and said, It is better for me to die than to live.
And God said to Jonah, Doest thou well to be angry for the gourd? And he said, I do well to be angry, even unto death.
Then said the Lord, Thou hast had pity on the gourd, for the which thou hast not laboured, neither madest it grow; which came up in a night, and perished in a night:
And should not I spare Nineveh, that great city, wherein are more than sixscore thousand persons that cannot discern between their right hand and their left hand; and also much cattle?
But he answered and said unto them, An evil and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign; and there shall no sign be given to it, but the sign of the prophet Jonas:
For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale’s belly; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.

He restored the coast of Israel from the entering of Hamath unto the sea of the plain, according to the word of the Lord God of Israel, which he spake by the hand of his servant Jonah, the son of Amittai, the prophet, which was of Gath–hepher.
